answer: The results ledger at command-center/bench/results/ledger.jsonl is append-only JSONL with a per-row content_hash chained through prev_hash/event_hash. Live row_count=24 verified in 0.000410s. Copies of that ledger: in-place edit, deleted row, and inserted row each DETECTED. Clean copy verifies silently (findings=0). 2 real concurrent writer processes appended 100 parseable records, chain_ok=True, torn_rows=0. SUCCESS:TST-0322

evidence.claim: Verifier detects in-place-edit, deleted-row and inserted-row on separate copies of the real ledger; clean copy is silent. row_count=24 wall_clock_s=0.000410.

evidence.claim: 2 concurrent OS processes wrote 100 intact JSONL rows in 0.2632s on linux; lock is O_CREAT|O_EXCL, not fcntl. Torn-tail copy is reported and repair names loss.

implementation.append: os.write of one canonical JSON line under ExclusiveLock, then fsync
implementation.locking: O_CREAT|O_EXCL lockfile; msvcrt.locking extra on win32

negative_controls.description: Payload mutated on a middle row of a ledger copy; content_hash/event_hash must fire.
A middle JSONL line removed from a copy.
A duplicate prior line spliced into a copy.
Final record truncated mid-line; verifier reports it and repair names how many records were lost.

notes: G-1 for TST-0322: live named probes must exit 0 against tools/bench/results_ledger.py. cloud ok=true is not delivery. Did not run global unit_manifest.py --write. Second Windows shell (pwsh7 / Git Bash) was not executed on this Linux substrate.
question_or_target: Implementation target: every number this program cites eventually traces to the results ledger, so a silently mutated past result poisons every downstream claim. Make the ledger append-only with a per-row content hash chained to the previous row, and ship the verifier that detects insertion, deletion and in-place edit.
